question: What is dry needling and how does it relieve pain?

Trigger point dry needling for tight muscles
answer: Dry needling involves inserting thin monofilament needles into myofascial trigger points (knots) to release deep muscle tension, improve blood flow, and alleviate pain. Unlike traditional acupuncture, dry needling is based on Western neuroanatomy.
answers: Dry needling involves inserting thin monofilament needles into myofascial trigger points (knots) to release deep muscle tension, improve blood flow, and alleviate pain. Unlike traditional acupuncture, dry needling is based on Western neuroanatomy.

Dry needling is a highly effective technique where a fine sterile needle is tapped into a hyper-irritable muscle knot (trigger point). This triggers a local twitch response that resets muscle tone, boosts circulation, and rapidly reduces chronic pain.

Key facts about dry needling:
• Purpose: Releases stubborn trigger points and deep muscle spasms
• Difference from acupuncture: Grounded in modern neuromuscular anatomy rather than Eastern meridians
• Sensation: Mild cramp or twitch sensation during treatment followed by profound muscle relaxation.

Every person heals at their own pace, but as a general guide, acute sprains or minor injuries often require 4 to 6 visits. More chronic issues or post-surgical cases typically take 8 to 12+ sessions. Your therapist will discuss exact timelines and milestones during your initial evaluation.

• Major surgeries & chronic issues: 10 – 16+ sessions with gradual home maintenance.
